newsitem.title: CANADA: Canadian bonds end weaker, eye on next week's data.
newsitem.headline: Canadian bonds end weaker, eye on next week's data.

text.p: Canadian bonds closed weaker on Friday, underperforming U.S. treasuries as a weaker currency and concern about U.S. economic data being released next week weighed on prices, analysts said.

"People are a little nervous about next week. There's a fear of what's coming out," said Garett Prins, a fixed-income analyst with J.P. Morgan Canada. "Stronger than expected results from any of these (U.S.) reports will send the market looking for another rate hike."
Canada's 30-year benchmark fell C$0.42 to C$107.60 to yield 7.341 percent.
The U.S. 30-year bond fell 4/32 to yield 7.14 percent. The spread between the two bonds widened to 20 basis points from 18 basis points at the close of trading on Thursday.

Canadian and U.S. bonds ended weaker amid concern about next week's U.S. employment cost, gross domestic product and payroll employment data. The reports are seen as a key indication of whether U.S. interest rates will rise further.

"It's just fear of next week's numbers. We've got some heavy hitters right from the start of the week and they culminate in the jobs data at the very end," said Jeoff Hall, Canadian analyst with Technical Data.

Concern about a possible rise in U.S. rates weighed on the Canadian dollar, which ended weaker at C$1.3970 (US$0.7158) from Thursday's close of C$1.3923 (US$0.7182). The dollar also weakened on expectations the Canadian government would call an election on Sunday.
Technical Data's Hall said Canada's underperformance resulted not so much from the currency's weakness as the fact that Canadian bonds outperformed U.S. treasuries in the past three sessions.
In other prices, the Canadian 10-year benchmark bond fell C$0.43 to C$101.25 to yield 6.819 percent. The U.S. bond fell 1/32 to yield 6.94 percent.
The negative spread between the bonds narrowed to 12 basis points from 18 basis points on Thursday.
The three-month cash T-bill yielded 3.17 percent against its U.S. equivalent, which yielded 5.30 percent.
